gloss: on time; on schedule; as scheduled

definitions.explanation: Exactly at the planned or expected time. Used to describe events, arrivals, departures, and actions happening as scheduled.

examples.japanese: {時間通|じかんどお}りに{着|つ}いた。
{電車|でんしゃ}は{時間通|じかんどお}りに{運行|うんこう}している。
examples.english: The trains are running on schedule.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}は{時間通|じかんどお}りに{始|はじ}まるので、{遅|おく}れないようにしてください。
examples.english: The meeting will start on time, so please make sure you're not late.

notes:
Composed of {時間|じかん} (time) + {通|どお}り (as, in accordance with). Literally means "as the time dictates" — i.e., at the appointed time.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間通|じかんどお}りに{来|く}る (to come on time)
- {時間通|じかんどお}りに{始|はじ}まる (to start on time)
- {時間通|じかんどお}りに{届|とど}く (to arrive on time [deliveries])
- {時間通|じかんどお}りに{進|すす}む (to proceed on schedule)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {定刻|ていこく}どおり — on the dot, at the appointed time; more formal, used for scheduled departure/arrival times
- {予定通|よていどお}り — as planned; broader, covering any kind of plan, not just time
- {時間|じかん}に{間|ま}に{合|あ}う — to be in time; focuses on making it before a deadline

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan's emphasis on punctuality makes {時間通|じかんどお}り a frequently used expression. Japanese trains are famously {時間通|じかんどお}り, and even slight delays prompt formal announcements and apologies.
